title: Linear-time bit appending
statement: For each Boolean value $b$, there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a natural number $c$ such that, on every Boolean input word $x$, $M$ computes the word obtained by appending $b$ to $x$ in time $c(|x|+1)$.
replaced:
For every fixed bit $b$ there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and a
constant $c$ such that $M$ computes the function $x \mapsto x b$ (append
the bit $b$ to the input word) within $c\,(n+1)$ steps on inputs of length
$n$.
